t: This is the Golders Green Hippodrome, built in 1913 as a music hall with three thousand seats. It was meant to serve North London, and in particular the new Northern line extension of the Underground into Golders Green. The architect was Bertie Crewe, one of the leading English theatre architects during the boom years between 1885 and 1915. So the scale of the building, and its link to the Tube, tell you something about how suburban entertainment grew with the railways.
